title: Soft-fallback orchestration and token handoff (tenant continuity) PRD - draft
body:
Summary:

This PRD proposes a Tenant Continuity Layer for Dedicated capacity: a soft-fallback orchestration that preserves customer-facing availability during transient capacity constraints by negotiating reduced-cost execution modes and exchanging short-lived capacity tokens between continuity pools. The design prioritizes continuity of inference requests with graceful degradation (bounded latency/quality tradeoffs), tenant isolation preservation, and auditable handoffs.

Problem statement:

Dedicated pools sometimes face unpredictable micro-surges (microbursts) that exceed provisioned SLOs. Current options: hard-throttle, preempt, or spill to hosted models. These are often either too disruptive (hard preemption) or too expensive (fallback to hosted). There is a need for a flexible, auditable soft-fallback mechanism that: 1) preserves user-visible availability, 2) minimizes unit cost and QoR regression, 3) maintains tenant isolation guarantees, and 4) provides operational observability.

Goals:
- Provide a runtime mechanism for ephemeral, constrained-quality fallbacks that keep requests served with bounded regressions in latency and output quality.
- Introduce a short-lived "continuity token" that represents ephemeral capacity rights and can be borrowed/returned between continuity pools under governed policies.
- Ensure fallbacks are policy-driven (per-tenant profile) and respect isolation rules (no noisy-neighbor escape).
- Deliver tooling: control-plane API, console UX, observability dashboards, and runbooks.

Non-goals:
- Replacing long-term reserved capacity commitments or replacing existing burst-credit models.
- Re-architecting model compilation or quantization pipelines (only operational knobs).

High-level design:

1) Continuity Pool and Tokens
- Continuity Pool: a logical pool in the control plane made of spare capacity segments (could be pre-warmed warm-pools or repurposed low-priority GPUs). Pools are region- and instance-class-aware.
- Continuity Token: a short-lived, auditable token (TTL 30s-5m configurable) that grants limited execution budget measured in token-units (example: 100 token-units ~ 1k tokens at typical gen rate). Tokens carry metadata: tenant, downgrade-profile, max-latency, audit-id.

2) Soft-fallback Profiles
- Each tenant can define 0..N profiles describing acceptable fallback behavior: e.g., model-variant (quantized/lo-res), pre-tokenized prefix caching, reduced max-length, or speculative sampling config. Profiles include SLO windows (max latency uplift %, allowed quality delta by eval metric).

3) Orchestration flow (runtime + control-plane)
- Detection: Serving runtime observes queue growth, KV-cache pressure, and headroom signals. When local pool cannot meet SLO, it signals the Continuity Orchestrator.
- Negotiation: Orchestrator consults tenant profile and available continuity pools. It attempts to allocate token(s) from a pool satisfying isolation constraints. Allocation uses a token ledger to record borrower/lender and audit-id.
- Execution: If token granted, request routed with fallback profile applied. Token-units are decremented atomically as the request is executed (continuity accounting).
- Return / Reconciliation: On completion or token TTL expiry, token accounting is reconciled. Excess token consumption can trigger soft-debt penalties (reduced future lending) or billing adjustments per policy.

Isolation & Safety rules:
- Lenders may opt-in per tenant namespace and set maximum outward lending caps.
- Tokens can only be allocated to tenants with compatible isolation profile (e.g., same security zone or allowed cross-tenant share list).
- Hard fences: if a tenant is flagged as sensitive or under strict SLA, their continuity tokens are only allowed from private pools or not allowed at all.
- Circuit-breaker: if a continuity pool’s lending rate exceeds safe thresholds, lending is suspended and fallback degrades to local preemption.

Control-plane APIs (examples)
- POST /v1/dedicated/continuity/pools - create/update pool (admin)
- GET /v1/dedicated/continuity/pools/{id}/tokens - view active tokens
- POST /v1/dedicated/continuity/tenants/{tenant}/profiles - create soft-fallback profile
- POST /v1/dedicated/continuity/allocate - runtime calls to request tokens (returns token & audit-id)
- POST /v1/dedicated/continuity/reconcile - reconcile usage and finalize ledger

Console UX (ops + tenant views)
- Ops view: pool occupancy, live token ledger, lending heatmap, incident toggles (suspend lending, quarantine pool).
- Tenant view: defined profiles, historical fallbacks, quality/latency impact graphs, token usage and billed adjustments.

Metrics & SLOs:
- Primary metrics: % requests served in-fallback vs normal, average latency uplift during fallback, quality delta by canary eval set, token consumption rate per minute.
- SLO targets (example): when continuity invoked, 95th latency uplift <= 40%, fallback quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) degradation <= 5% compared to baseline.

Operational runbook (short):
- Trigger: Autoscaler fails to meet SLO for >2 minutes and continuity pool lending >30% -> page SRE on-call.
- Immediate actions: inspect token ledger, check pool circuit-breakers, suspend lending if error rate >5% in fallback requests.
- Post-mortem signals: large sustained token debt, repeated cross-tenant lending on sensitive pools.

Billing and policy implications:
- Default: Continuity usage billed at discounted rate relative to on-demand hosted fallback but higher than tenant reserved rate. Billing rules configurable per customer contract.
- Soft-debt handling: if a tenant consumes tokens beyond negotiated limits, flag for review and enable throttled recoveries.

Monitoring & Auditing:
- Every token allocation, execution, and reconciliation is recorded in the continuity ledger (immutable audit-id). Ledger available via API for customer auditing and internal compliance.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (Q1): Simulation mode - orchestration simulated in staging using traffic replay and no-live lending. Add dashboarding and ledger schema. (JIRA: INF-4321)
- Phase 1 (Q2): Opt-in tenants + limited regions - enable lending from shared non-sensitive pools, collect metrics, validate profiles.
- Phase 2 (Q3): Full GA - include per-contract billing, console controls, and default safety policies.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How to formalize quality-degradation metrics usable across diverse tenant workloads? (need lightweight per-tenant eval harness)
- Token economics and how to present soft-debt semantics in billing UX.
- Runtime atomicity guarantees for token unit decrement across sharded request executions.

Next steps / action items:
- Engineering spike (2w) to prototype token ledger and allocation API (owner: Marco Li)
- SRE run test: design chaos tests that simulate pool unreliability and token TTL expirations (owner: Leah)
- Product: finalize fallback profile schema and sample defaults (owner: Rina)
- Legal/customer success: draft contract language for opt-in continuity usage and data handling notes.

Appendix: quick glossary
- Continuity Pool: logical set of spare capacity for soft-fallbacks.
- Continuity Token: short-lived permission unit with usage accounting.
- Fallback Profile: tenant-configured rules that constrain the type and extent of soft-degradation allowed.

Notes: This document deliberately focuses on the orchestration and governance layer rather than underlying model optimization. The goal is to deliver a predictable, auditable, and controllable continuity experience that reduces hard-failures without compromising tenant isolation or compliance.
